verdict.line: You lose this if you let Nasus farm freely to level 6 and beyond and his Siphoning Strike stacks catch up to your flat damage; you win it if you force all-ins before he hits 6, while his Q is on cooldown and he has no answer to your E's knockup.

brief.thesis: Camille's trade package peaks before level 6 and decays afterward relative to Nasus's stacking Q, which is exactly why the measured numbers show Camille holding lane and solo-kill advantage but the head-to-head win rate sitting at 49.8% over 1596 games — an overall even matchup. The entire game plan is converting your early structural edge into a lead before Nasus's Fury of the Sands and compounding Siphoning Strike stacks let him scale past you.

theirWindow.when: Nasus hits 6, Fury of the Sands ready
theirWindow.what: Once Nasus has his R (Fury of the Sands, 120s cooldown) available, a sustained fight lets him gain bonus health, attack range, and drain your max health into bonus damage for the duration. Don't chain-trade in melee range during this window — disengage and reset instead of fighting through his sandstorm.

yourWindow.when: levels 3-5, before his Q stacks snowball
yourWindow.what: With E (Hookshot, 16/15/14/13/12s cooldown, range 800) up and a wall nearby, pull in and knock him up, then follow with an empowered Q (Precision Protocol) auto and stand at W (Tactical Sweep) outer range after the cast delay for the slow, bonus damage, and heal. Time these all-ins for when his Siphoning Strike (8/7/6/5/4s cooldown) is on cooldown and he can't contest or stack safely — this is OP.GG's own read on the matchup and it's correct.

start.why: Run with Health Potion; this is the dominant start at 50.8% win rate over 1648 games and the sustained-damage profile matches your melee trade pattern better than a shield start into a champion whose poke is a short-range Q, not ranged harass.

boots.why: 51.3% win rate over 947 games; Nasus's damage is entirely basic-attack and Siphoning Strike based, and Steelcaps' flat damage reduction against his autos is more valuable here than Mercury's Treads' tenacity, since his only slow (Wither) is a secondary concern next to his auto-attack trading.

core.why: First item on the highest-win-rate path (58.6% over 413 games); the move speed and empowered auto synergize with your E-engage, Q-empower combo to win the short trade windows before his R.
Second item on the same path; sustain and cleave let you win extended trades and farm/wave-clear to match Nasus's stacking tempo.
Completes the top-performing core (58.6% win rate, 43.8% pick); the damage-over-time conversion blunts the burst from a stacked Siphoning Strike or a Spirit Fire-amplified auto.

runes.keystoneWhy: This page runs at 48.9% win rate with 22.4% pick rate, the more popular of the two measured setups; the proc rewards the exact trade pattern this matchup calls for — standing in range while he farms with Q, stacking max health that both outlasts his poke and fuels the all-in once your E knockup lands.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is the most-picked combo (68.9% pick, 51.1% win rate) and pairs with your level 3-5 all-in window — Ignite punishes his lack of a dash or disengage before Wither comes up. Teleport+Ignite measures higher at 55% win rate over fewer games if you'd rather prioritize scaling into side-lane splitpush, which fits if you expect the lane to go even and want to win the game through map pressure instead.

playing.title: Punish his Q stacking window
playing.detail: Engage when Nasus's Siphoning Strike (8/7/6/5/4s cooldown) is down and he can't contest a trade or safely take the last hit he needs to stack. This is the single highest-value habit in the matchup.

playing.title: Hookshot off lane walls for knockups
playing.detail: E (Hookshot, range 800) needs a wall to pull to — identify the nearest one before you commit to a trade so the knockup is available on demand, not just when you happen to be standing next to terrain.

playing.title: Fight from W's outer edge
playing.detail: Tactical Sweep's outer half slows and deals extra damage while healing you; after the cast delay, position so his melee range only reaches your Q and basic attacks, not a counter-trade.

playing.title: Don't stand in Spirit Fire
playing.detail: Nasus's E (12s cooldown, range 650) reduces the armor of anyone standing in the flame zone; disengage out of it rather than facetanking through your armor-heavy Trinity/Hydra build.

playing.title: Respect level 6 onward
playing.detail: Once Fury of the Sands (120s cooldown) is up, a prolonged fight lets him gain health, range, and max-health drain damage — take short trades and reset instead of committing fully.

playing.title: Buy antiheal if he's snowballed
playing.detail: Soul Eater's bonus lifesteal scales with his stacks; Executioner's Calling directly answers a Nasus who's pulled ahead on farm.

playing.title: Convert your lead into side pressure
playing.detail: Your measured lane and solo-kill advantage is real but time-limited — if you're ahead by level 5, push plates and force him to choose between matching your tempo and continuing to farm stacks.

brief.patchCaveat: Every build path, rune page, summoner spell, and win rate here is measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG — none of it is estimated. The level ranges, cooldown citations, and tactical reasoning connecting those numbers to specific trade windows are this brief's own analysis, not sourced data.
